Why study with us in Oxford?

The most popular summer school in Oxford since 2004.

Sleep in the rooms, dine in the halls and cross the quads that shaped 30 British prime ministers and more than 70 Nobel laureates. For two weeks, this is where you live.

It was here that Academy Royale International began with a vision: to create an exceptional academic summer in Oxford’s historic college settings. More than 20 years and 50,000 alumni later, students still come to explore future degree subjects, experience university-style teaching and find the confidence and direction to shape their future.

Accredited and multi award-winning summer schools

The Student Experience in Oxford

Oxford is not a backdrop. It is a world students step into.

Imagine studying where Nobel laureates once dreamed and the world's greatest literary works were born. Study and stay in Oxford colleges where every hall, quad and courtyard is a living lesson in greatness. Explore a city steeped in history, discoveries and timeless magic.

Faculty

Meet the experts in their fields

Unlike other summer programmes, our curriculum is designed and developed by academic experts who draw from their wealth of experience, crafting programmes that help students grasp core concepts, develop critical-thinking skills, enlighten them on the current issues and innovations shaping the future of their subject.

Dr Amy Booth

University of Oxford

Medicine

Co-director of the Green Healthcare Hub and a DPhil Rhodes Scholar at the University of Oxford. Runs the Oxford course on Sustainable Health Care and is co-authoring a forthcoming book on the subject.

Lavanya Rajamani

University of Oxford

Law

Yamani Fellow in Public International Law at St Peter’s College. DPhil and BCL at Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar; LLM, Yale. Formerly Director of Studies in Law at Queens’ College, Cambridge.

Digby Chappell

University of Oxford

Engineering

Associate Professor of Engineering Science at the University of Oxford, a member of the Oxford Robotics Institute and Tutorial Fellow at St Anne’s College. He leads the HEAT Lab, developing body-interfacing technologies designed to restore and enhance human abilities.

Dr Charmaine Lang

University of Oxford

Biotechnology & Genetics

Oxford-GSK IMCM Fellow and Group Leader in the Nuffield Department of Medicine at the University of Oxford. Her research focuses on glial-neuron interactions in Parkinson’s disease, using advanced cellular, transcriptomic and imaging approaches to identify potential disease-modifying therapeutic targets.

Lily Mainwaring

University of Oxford

Medicine

Lily Mainwaring is an NIHR Academic Clinical Fellow in General Surgery at the University of Oxford. Her research focuses on surgical quality assurance, technical performance, training and patient safety. She studied Natural Sciences and Medicine at Cambridge, graduating with a First-Class degree and Distinction in Medicine alongside several academic prizes. She is also involved in undergraduate medical teaching at Oxford and supports students considering careers in medicine and surgery.

Dr Nikita Hari

University of Oxford

Engineering

Head of the Teaching and Research Design Group in the Department of Engineering Science at the University of Oxford. She holds a doctorate in Electrical Engineering from Cambridge and has more than a decade of experience across industry and higher education.

Hanna Adeyema

MIT

MIT Future Builders

Hannah is the Director MIT Open Learning and is passionate about technology, entrepreneurship, health, and education. She began her career at a DC think tank researching technology trends after completing her MBA at the MIT Sloan School of Management, undertaking projects in collaboration with the MIT Media Lab.

Dr Claire Keene

University of Oxford

Medicine

Claire is a public health clinician with a Master’s in International Health and Tropical Medicine from the University of Oxford. Amongst her many achievements, she managed an HIV and tuberculosis project for Médecins Sans Frontières in Khayelitsha, South Africa, leading the project’s COVID response in 2020.

How students learn

A curriculum developed over 20 years

This is not two weeks with one teacher. Our curriculum, honed over more than 20 summers, mirrors the variety and intellectual rhythm of university learning. Students encounter several specialist voices, interrogate ideas with their class lecturer, apply their knowledge and learn to present conclusions with confidence.

01

Learn from several specialists.

Guest lecturers bring current expertise from academia and professional life. A Business student might hear separately from a founder, a seed-funding specialist and a social-media strategist, gaining perspectives that one teacher alone cannot provide.

02

Question, connect and debate.

The class lecturer helps students interrogate each expert perspective through seminars, tutorials and structured discussion. Students learn to test assumptions, compare viewpoints and build arguments rather than simply absorb information.

03

Turn knowledge into judgement.

Students apply ideas through practical challenges, from pitching a business or performing CPR to debating a case or solving a real problem, before presenting and defending their work. This develops judgement, communication, collaboration and confidence.

Your Oxford Campus

Live, dine and study in a historic Oxford college.

Students stay at Balliol College, St Peter’s College and St Catherine’s College, experiencing daily life in spaces shaped by generations of scholars, world leaders, pioneering thinkers and Nobel Prize winners.

Beyond the classroom

An unforgettable summer

Excursions, socials, sport and a graduation night, filling the hours between lectures.

An unforgettable summer

Exploring Oxford is like stepping into your very own fairytale. Our fully-supervised trips bring the magic of the city to life through guided tours, college visits, riverside walks, and hidden gems. We also offer an optional London trip for those craving a bigger adventure.

  • Guided walking tours around historic Oxford landmarks
  • Visits to iconic colleges, libraries, and heritage sites
  • Exploration of local markets, scenic quads, and riverside paths
  • Engaging stories from expert guides who know Oxford inside out
  • Optional full-day London excursion for an unforgettable city experience

Forge Friendships from Around the World

Our social programme is all about connection, creativity, and giving students the confidence to try new things. From punting and hands-on workshops to debate evenings, gallery visits, and relaxed welcome events, there's something to inspire everyone.

  • Punting on the Cherwell with friends
  • Creative workshops designed to spark imagination and confidence
  • Debate society evenings for big ideas and bold voices
  • Karaoke, talent shows and fashion workshops
  • Visits to museums, galleries, the Covered Market, and Westgate
  • Friendly welcome activities to help everyone settle in quickly

Enjoy your favourites, or try something new

Our sessions channel Oxford’s strong sports heritage: lively, inclusive, and full of friendly competition. Whether students are into team sports or want to try something new, they’ll enjoy everything from football tournaments to classic English lawn games and our very own park "Olympics."

  • Football tournaments for all skill levels
  • Badminton matches and fast-paced mini-games
  • Morning run club
  • Traditional English lawn games
  • Capture-the-flag sessions that get everyone moving
  • "Olympics in the Park" with a mix of challenges

End Your Summer in Style

Our graduation celebration is a wonderful way to end every experience. Held in a beautiful Oxford college, it brings everyone together to celebrate their achievements. Enjoy an exclusive formal dinner, before dancing the night away at our midsummer graduation party.

  • Graduation ceremony in a historic Oxford location
  • Recognition of achievements and programme milestones
  • Formal dinner in a classic Oxford dining hall
  • Celebration with teachers, friends, and peers
  • Graduation party to mark an unforgettable final night

Frequently Asked Questions

Questions families ask about Oxford

Academy Royale International’s summer school in Oxford is a two-week residential academic programme for students aged 12–18. Students live and learn in historic Oxford college settings, explore their chosen subjects through university-style teaching and enjoy a full programme of activities, excursions and social events.

No. Academy Royale International is an independent summer-school provider that has been running programmes on campus at the University of Oxford since 2004. We contract with colleges of the University of Oxford for the use of their accommodation, dining, teaching and event facilities, but our programmes are not operated, authorised, endorsed or taught by the University of Oxford.

Our summer school in Oxford is open to students aged 12–18. Students study in age-appropriate classes, with programmes and pastoral arrangements designed separately for students aged 12–15 and 16–18.

Each Oxford programme lasts two weeks. The 2027 sessions run from 4–17 July, 18–31 July and 1–15 August. Students can also combine consecutive sessions to stay for four or six weeks.

Students can choose from a wide range of subjects, including Medicine, Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Business, Law, Economics, Architecture, Psychology, Biotechnology, Creative Writing and Sustainability. We also offer multi-subject programmes for students who want to explore several interests during their summer.

Students stay in accommodation at Balliol College, St Peter’s College or St Catherine’s College and other colleges are added when needed. They experience daily life in historic Oxford college settings, with lessons in inspiring classrooms, meals in college dining halls and access to college grounds and facilities.

Families can enrol through our secure online booking system. A deposit of £1,295 per two-week session is required to secure a place, with the remaining balance due no later than 90 days before the programme begins. After enrolment, families receive access to the Academy Royale International Portal, where they can manage payments and submit important student information.

College allocation depends on the student’s age, chosen programme, session and accommodation availability. Families may submit accommodation requests, but a particular college or room cannot be guaranteed unless confirmed in writing.

Oxford accommodation includes a mixture of single and twin bedrooms. Students can request a particular room type, but requests are subject to availability. Some locations may also offer an en-suite room reservation for an additional fee.

Yes. Male and female students are accommodated on separate corridors or staircases. Different age groups are also housed separately wherever possible, reflecting the different welfare and safeguarding arrangements for students aged 12–15 and 16–18.

Student safety is supported by trained residential staff, controlled campus access, 24-hour security arrangements and clear sign-in, sign-out and curfew procedures. Students are accompanied by staff during organised lessons, activities and excursions, and every campus has a 24-hour emergency contact number.

Students must sign out and back in whenever they leave campus. Students aged 12–15 may only leave in groups of at least three, while students aged 16–18 may leave in pairs. Younger students have earlier curfews and tighter limits on independent time.

Each Oxford campus is led by an experienced Programme Director and supported by trained residential, academic, events and welfare staff. Team members are available throughout the programme to help students settle in, remain safe and make the most of their experience.

Our faculty includes academics, and researchers at leading universities such as the University of Oxford and practising professionals with extensive experience in their field. Students learn from several specialist voices as well as a class lecturer who guides their seminars, discussions, practical work and presentations.

Students attending an academic programme should have approximately C1-level English or an IELTS score of 6.5 or above. Students who have attended an English-speaking school for two or more years are exempt from the formal English-language requirement.

Morning classes typically run from 09:00 to 12:30. Afternoon academic sessions usually take place on three or four days each week, followed by activities, excursions, guest lectures or social events. Exact schedules vary by programme and day.

Students enjoy a varied programme of cultural activities, sports and social events. These may include punting, Oxford walking tours, college and museum visits, creative workshops, debate evenings, football, talent shows and a formal graduation celebration.

Breakfast and dinner are included for all Oxford students. Lunch is also included for students aged 12–15. Students aged 16–18 can explore Oxford’s cafés, restaurants and markets at lunchtime and should budget approximately £10 per day for lunch.

We can accommodate most dietary and support requirements when informed in advance. Families must provide details of allergies, medical conditions, disabilities, medication and learning differences through the secure student portal. Where appropriate, an Individual Student Support Agreement may be created with the family.

Yes. Academy Royale International offers an optional supervised airport transfer service for an additional fee. London Heathrow, Gatwick, Stansted and Luton are the most convenient international airports for Oxford. However students wishing to take the transfer service need to arrive and depart from Heathrow. Eligible airports, travel windows and booking instructions are provided before arrival.

A summer that changes everything

Dive into AI this summer

Academy Royale International’s Artificial Intelligence Summer School opens your eyes to the possibilities of AI while giving you the skills to harness it in the future.

Over two weeks, you will learn from instructors from TechSpark, a leading EduTech organisation, through fascinating classes and hands-on practical challenges.

The film

Two weeks in ninety seconds

See the classes, college halls and students who found their purpose on our programmes.

an innovative curriculum

Future-focused learning delivered by experts

Week one · Foundations

Get Up to Speed with AI

This module introduces you to AI: what it is, how it differs from traditional programming, and why it has become so important so quickly. Learning from everyday examples and practical tasks, you will be introduced to key concepts including algorithms, data and pattern recognition. Hands-on tasks might include using Google’s Teachable Machine to train an ML model or recognise hand-drawn digits, or interpreting a pre-built dataset.

Machine learning is a type of AI which lets computers find patterns in data to learn from it, meaning computers get better at tasks the more they learn. In this module, you will engage with practical examples and discussions to explore the different ways AI can learn, including supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning. You will consider how these methods can influence the behaviours and accuracy of AI models.

Natural language processing (NLP) combines computational linguistics, machine learning and statistical models to understand and generate human language. You will examine how AI systems process text and speech to translate, summarise text and generate conversation. Through real-world examples including chatbots and translation software, you will discover how NLP transforms computer processing into human communication.

Computer vision involves computers interpreting visual information from images and videos. You will discover how AI systems recognise objects and patterns through case studies including face recognition technology, social media filters and self-driving cars. By the end of the module, you will understand how pixels, pattern recognition and neural networks combine to enable Computer Vision.

Week two · Developing Skills

Look Towards the Future

In this module you will examine case studies from manufacturing, exploration and service industries to understand how AI enables robots to make decisions and interact with their environments. You will deepen your understanding of how sensors, data and intelligent algorithms are integrated to perform tasks, and the impact of this on the human workforce.

This module brings your AI learning into the real world, bringing together everything you have learned so far and applying it to industry contexts. This includes healthcare, finance, transportation and entertainment. You will reflect on the opportunities and challenges of AI, and speculate on how it will continue to develop and influence the future.

This module looks at the AI developments of the future, asking how AI's continues development poses opportunities and risks to society and technology. You will examine how generative AI can be used to create deepfakes, AI-generated art and other creative content, assessing their benefits and the risks they can pose to human artists. You will also examine how transformers have revolutionised large language models.

You will probably have seen news articles and been involved in conversions with friends and family about the ethics of AI. This module gives you an opportunity to discuss ethical uses of AI at length, discussing issues such as privacy concerns, bias in algorithms and the impact of AI on employment and the environment. You will learn why responsible development and regulation are essential for the future of AI.

Learn AI in Practice

Get ahead on the skills of the future

With the help of TechSpark experts, you will apply everything you learn to real-world challenges which culminate in a Practical Project. You can choose between coding and non-coding options, allowing you to develop your skills in an area of your choosing.

Over the course of two weeks, you will gain a range of impressive new skills.

  • Develop your use of various software tools and coding programmes
  • Stretch your critical thinking skills by comparing different kinds of machine learning
  • Improve transferable skills for maths and science subjects by analysing data sets
  • Develop your debating and argumentation skills as you discuss the ethics of AI

Learning outcomes

By the end, you will be able to:

You will leave Academy Royale International with a new understanding of how AI works and its uses in technology and industry.

You will have become an informed, responsible AI user with transferrable skills which are valuable across computer science and other fields

The Practical Project is a chance to pursue an area which interests you in more depth, building practical AI skills alongside expertise in related areas. You will create a project which demonstrates your learning, and can even become the basis of a future university application. Previous examples include:

  • Train Your First AI Model: Experience how AI learns in real time, and gain the skills to ensure a successful model
  • Deepfake & Misinformation Analysis: Explore how AI generated content can be used for fake news, and develop strategies to detect manipulated content
  • Bias Detection in AI: Choose to use coding or code-free methods to identify biased datasets and redesign them for fairness and accuracy
  • AI for Good Project: Develop business skills including leadership alongside your tech expertise by designing and pitching an AI solution to a real-world problem

Faculty & speakers

Taught by experts from Techspark

Academy Royale International’s Artificial Intelligence course is taught by an expert faculty including experts from Techspark, a leading technology education specialist.

Bipasha Goyal

EPFL

Bipasha is a Life Sciences Engineering Masters student at EPFL with a background in Biomedical Systems Engineering from the University of Toronto. Her technical portfolio spans impactful biomedical innovations, ranging from developing LumineSense - a smart UV disinfection device designed to neutralize pathogens like COVID-19 - to leading computational cancer research at the Princess Margaret Cancer Centre and SickKids Hospital, alongside advanced biomaterial and drug delivery research at the Shoichet Lab.

Alvin Walker

ETH Zurich and University of Zurich

Alvin combines a rigorous academic background in Health Science and Technology at ETH and Biostatistics at University of Zurich, with proven leadership as a Swiss Armed Forces Officer. A dedicated teacher with years of experience developing and delivering innovative tech courses, such as Python, AI and Cybersecurity. Alvin expertly guides students through complex topics with ease, blending technical precision with engaging, hands-on mentorship.

Rodrigue de Guerre

EPFL

Rodrigue is a technology entrepreneur working across artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and software engineering. He has helped build Melødia, an AI music platform combining generative AI with secure passwordless authentication, and is part of the team behind Hypto, a technology startup developing digital tools for the construction sector. Alongside his entrepreneurial work, Rodrigue studies Electrical Engineering and Cybersecurity at EPFL and has extensive experience teaching and mentoring young developers.

Archibald Lecointre

EPFL

Archibald is an EPFL Energy Master’s student and President of the Swiss Solar Boat team in Lausanne, Switzerland. Leading 75 students in building a revolutionary hydrogen-solar foiler, Archie is an expert in sustainable engineering. He inspires students to build green technologies with AI tools and lead the renewable energy transition.

Yassine Taoudi-Benchekroun

ETH Zurich

Yassine Taoudi-Benchekroun is a PhD researcher at the Institute of Neuroinformatics at ETH Zurich. His research bridges machine learning, cognitive science, and neuroscience, investigating computational mechanisms of compositionality and out-of-distribution generalization in artificial neural architectures. A dedicated educator, he develops custom interactive curricula and teaches programming and machine learning to diverse audiences, integrating accessible pedagogy with complex technical concepts.

AI Summer School FAQs

Everything families need to know

Detailed answers for parents and students comparing AI summer schools.

This programme is designed for curious, engaged students who are excited to spend part of their summer developing their understanding of AI. It is perfect for students who already enjoy learning about science and technology, and want to stretch their learning beyond the classroom and apply it to the real world.

No previous knowledge of AI, computer science or coding is needed. While coding skills are great, all modules come with coding-free options for students who are new to the subject. No knowledge of AI theory or practical use is needed, and software access is provided.

The course is designed to push bright students to take on new academic challenges by introducing lots of new concepts and practical tasks. While students are stretched, their learning is guided by expert members of our faculty and takes place in small classes, ensuring that every student feels supported and enjoys their learning while encountering new ideas.

While students do not need to be sure what they want to study in the future, some students will already be set on a university course. For students already considering how an Academy Royale International Exploring Artificial Intelligence Summer School can shape their future, the course is the perfect first step towards university applications. Students have the opportunity to ask their tutors and industry professionals for application advice. They also receive a certificate, grades and a report which make excellent supporting materials for a strong university application.

The course is very hands-on. Each module involves practical demonstrations and tasks, and the final Practical Project is a chance for students to immerse themselves in an extended piece of hands-on work. Students enjoy consolidating their learning through these practical challenges and getting to know their classmates during team challenges.

A typical morning involves a lecture and two seminars or workshops. In the afternoon students have another extended workshop or practical session. The rest of the day is spent socialising with friends during activities, enjoying delicious meals in inspiring campus settings and exploring the city.

The programme takes place in the inspiring campuses of the Universities of Oxford. Students have access to university-level facilities and teaching spaces.

By teaching in small groups, we ensure that each student has a personalised relationship with their tutor. This means they receive high-quality constructive feedback and any support they need in class. It also means that students bond with their classmates, creating a friendly atmosphere in which students get involved and ask questions with confidence.

Our students come from all over the world. Since our first summer school in 2004, we have welcomed students from over 175 countries. They speak a wide range of languages and come from a wide range of backgrounds, creating a vibrant community perfect for international students.

At the end of the course, students receive a graduation pack which contains a certificate acknowledging their academic achievements during the course. They also receive a personalised report and detailed grades.

Explore AI insights

A helpful guide for students considering AI at Academy Royale International and beyond

Is Explore Artificial Intelligence the right subject for me?

AI is the technology of the future, and is already shaping our world. The course is technical, but backs up this computing knowledge with practical demonstrations and engaging challenges. Ask yourself these questions to determine if Explore Artificial Intelligence is the right course for you.
  • Do I enjoy learning about science and technology?
  • Am I curious about the uses, challenges and future of AI?
  • Have I got an enthusiasm for working in teams to solve complex issues?
  • Am I willing to get stuck into new challenges and tasks?
Read More

What will I learn?

At an Academy Royale International Summer School, we bring learning to life by taking it beyond the classroom. You will leave with a new appreciation for the place of AI in the modern world and your own abilities to use it.
  • The foundations of AI including algorithms, data and pattern recognition
  • How AI turns data into output, including Natural Language Processing and GenAI
  • The application of AI to real-world uses including robotics and chatbots
  • Ethical debates around the responsible use of AI
Read More

How should I choose a location?

Each of our locations delivers serious academic study within an inspiring campus. Choose your perfect location according to the setting, atmosphere and dates which suit you best. These are some questions to ask yourself when choosing.
  • Would I prefer the busy atmosphere of Oxford or the more peaceful and scholarly atmosphere of Cambridge?
  • Which dates on offer fit with the rest of my summer plans?
  • Which city am I the most excited to explore with an international community of new friends?
